//ServerUrl: Loopback on purpose - the application has no authentication. Change the port if it is taken, not the host.
//DataDirectory: Empty means the platform's local application data folder. Set it to keep the library on another drive.
//Engine: Internal tuning. Every value below is also the code default, so deleting this whole section changes nothing. Anything the user is meant to change - prompts, models, output ceiling, voice window, timeouts - lives in the database and is edited from the settings screen instead.

Engine.//batching: How a chapter is cut into requests.

batching.//maxCharacters: Secondary guard beside the token budget, for when the token estimate is wrong.
batching.//safetyMargin: Tokens held back from the output ceiling so a slightly long reply still lands.
batching.//minimumTokens: Floor on the budget. Lower turns one chapter into hundreds of requests.
batching.//maxAttempts: Tries at the segment format before the batch is halved and retried.
batching.//carryParagraphs: Tail of the previous batch carried forward so the voice holds across a split chapter.

Engine.//glossary: Term matching and how far the glossary looks for an established rendering.

glossary.//maxCandidateChapters: Chapters examined when looking for a term in an existing translation.
glossary.//alignmentWindow: Paragraphs either side to consider when the two sides do not line up.
glossary.//maxInflectionLength: Letters that may follow a term and still be the same word. Raise it for a language with longer case endings than Russian or German.
glossary.//maxTermLength: Above this a returned term is a model explaining itself, not a name.

checks.//minimumResidueRun: Consecutive source-script letters before it counts as a skipped fragment rather than a name left in its original spelling.
checks.//minimumBlockLength: Below this an identical line is not evidence of a copied block.
checks.//maxReported: Issues reported per check before it stops counting.

chat.//historyTurns: Messages replayed to the agent each turn.

Engine.//models: The model dropdown. The CLI has no command that lists its catalogue, so this list is configured rather than discovered - aliases by default, because an alias always resolves to the newest model of its family and so does not go stale. Add an entry to reach a model released after this build. Local models are not listed here: they are fetched live from the configured server.

models.label: Sonnet
models.description: The working default. Strong literary judgement at a fraction of Opus's cost, and what a full-length book is realistically translated with.

models.label: Opus
models.description: The most capable, and by a wide margin the most expensive. Worth it for a difficult passage or a book whose prose carries it; wasteful across thousands of pages.

models.label: Haiku
models.description: Fast and cheap. Suited to the glossary's mechanical work - listing proper nouns, reading back how a term was rendered - rather than to prose.

models.label: Fable
models.description: Tuned for creative writing, which is closer to what a novel translation actually is than general assistance.
